newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fruit, govt rates push up Australia CPI.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fruit, govt rates push up Australia CPI.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Statistics said fruit prices and local government rates had had the strongest upward effect on Australia's consumer price index in the September quarter.

"Contributing most to the overall increase this quarter were prices of fresh fruit (up 10.1 percent), local government rates and charges (up 2.2 percent), hospital and medical services (up 1.3 percent), urban transport fares (up 3.3 percent), the cost of entertainment (up 1.6 percent), vehicle insurance (up 1.5 percent), the price of bread (up 3.6 percent) and privately owned dwelling rents (up 0.8 percent)," the bureau said.
Falling mortgage interest charges and prices for petrol, cars and furniture offset the rises, the bureau said.
The government forecast a 2.0 percent year-average rise in the consumer price index for the year to June 1997.
This will be achieved if the remaining three quarters of the fiscal year average a 0.5 or 0.6 percent quarterly rise.

The underlying inflation measure, which rose 0.5 percent in the September quarter, can now average quarterly rises of 0.8 or 0.9 percent for the rest of the fiscal year and still not exceed the 1996/97 year-average forecast of 2.75 percent.
National Australian economist Jeff Oughton said that was unlikely. "We're on track for a number much better than in the budget," he told Reuters.
